questions.question: Which famous Rashtrakuta king built the rock-cut temple of Kailash at Ellora?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **Rashtrakuta King Krishna I.**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**__Krishna I__

__
 
• He conquered the territories that were still under the Chalukyas
 
• He also occupied Konkan.
 
• Krishna I also defeated Vishnuvardhana of Vengi and the Ganga king of Mysore.
 
• He was a great patron of art and architecture.
 
• The Kailash Temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta King Krishna I.
 
• The Kailasa temple (Cave 16) is the largest of the 34 Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu cave temples and monasteries located along the sloping basalt cliff at Ellora Caves.
 
• Generally, most of the excavation was completed by Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (r. c. 756 - 773) in the eighth century, although some elements were added later. 

 [IMAGE: https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/66499582.cms?resizemode=75&width=1200&height=900] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __Govinda III (793 - 814)__

__
 
• The Rashtrakuta king who defeated the Pratihara ruler Nagabhatta II was Govinda III
 
• Pala King Dharmapala and his protégé Charayudh sought the help of Govinda III.
 
• His kingdom spread up to the Vindhyas and Malava in the north and the river Tungabhadra to the south.
 
• Govind III's northern campaign was not for empire expansion but for fame.
 
• Govind III defeated Pratihara king Nagabhatta II in 793 - 814 AD.
 
• Govind III further defeated the Pallava king Dantivarman in 803 at Kanchi.

**Jai Chand:**

 
• King Jai Chand__ was defeated by **Muhammad Ghori **in the Battle of Chandawar.
 
• The **Battle of Chandwar** took place between **1193 and 1194 CE.**
 
• **Prithviraj Chauhan** was the king of **Chauhan dynasty**, reigns between **1178 to 1192 CE.**
 
• Bhima II was a member of the **Chaulukya or Solanki dynasty**, reigns between **1178 to 1240 CE**.
 
• Kumarpala was an Indian king from the Chaulukya or Solanki dynasty of Gujarat reigns between **1143 to 1172 CE.**

questions.question: The Kamakshi Saunsthan temple of Goa is crowned with the ______ two-storied tower and with a golden Kalash perched on its Shikhar.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**octagonal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kamakshi Saunsthan Temple** is one of the renowned temples in the state of **Goa**, dedicated to the deity **Kamakshi Devi**.
 
• The temple is adorned with an **octagonal two-storied tower**, which is a distinctive architectural feature.
 
• The **octagonal tower** symbolizes a unique and intricate design often seen in Indian temple architecture, adding to the temple's grandeur.
 
• A **golden Kalash** is perched on the **Shikhar** (the topmost point of the temple), further highlighting the temple's sacredness and importance.
 
• Such architectural elements are typical in temples across India, where the structures are designed to reflect **cultural and spiritual significance**.
 
• The **Kamakshi Saunsthan Temple** serves as a center for spiritual and cultural activities and attracts devotees from various regions.
 
• The presence of an **octagonal tower** in the architecture signifies balance and symmetry, which are essential elements of traditional Indian temple construction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pentagonal**__

 __
 
• **Pentagonal structures** are less common in traditional Indian temple architecture but are used in modern designs or other cultural monuments worldwide.
 
• They are often associated with **geometric balance** and can be seen in fortifications or other architectural structures.
 
 
 
• **Circular**__
 __
 
• **Circular structures** are occasionally used in Indian temples, often representing **eternity and completeness**.
 
• These designs are more typical in stupas or Buddhist architecture rather than Hindu temples.
 
 
 
• **Hexagonal**__
 
 
• **Hexagonal designs** are rare in Indian temple architecture, as most traditional structures prefer symmetry through square or octagonal shapes.
 
• Hexagons are more common in modern designs or specific cultural monuments that emphasize **structural uniqueness**.

questions.question: Which of the following architectural styles had an entrance gateway called 'Gopuram'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Dravidian architecture**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Most of the important temples present in the South Indian states have a gopuram.

 
 
• Gopuram acts as a characteristic feature to represent the temples built in the Dravidian Style.
 
 
 
• The entrance gateway in the Dravidian style of temples is known as Gopuram.
 
• The finest examples of their architecture are the Chennakesava Temple in Belur, the Hoysaleswara Temple in Halebid, and the Kesava Temple in Somanathapura. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/234180df17cbf574b669bafac323f507da6d889f84161537348eda55de9df82e.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

**Buddhist architecture:**

 
• Buddhist Architecture is primarily represented by three prominent building types:

 
 
• The Chaitya Hall (Place Of Worship or Prayer hall)
 
• The Vihara (Monastery)
 
• The Stupa (Hemispherical Mound For Worship/Memory)
 
 
 
• Chaitya is a place of worship, while Vihara is the dwelling place of the monks.
 
• Both early Chaityas and Viharas were made from woods and later stone-cut Chaityas and Viharas were made.
 
• Chaitya was a rectangular prayer hall with a stupa placed in the centre, the purpose was prayer.
 
• The Chaitya was divided into three parts and had an apsidal ending, that is, a semicircular rear end.
 
• The central part of the hall (also called the nave) was separated from the two aisles by two rows of pillars.
 
• The chaityas also had polished interior walls, semicircular roofs and horse-shoe-shaped windows called the Chaitya windows.
 
• Viharas were the residences of the monks.
 
• ​Distinctive Buddhist architectural structures and sculptures like Stupas, Pagodas, caves, and monasteries
 
• Being the spiritual symbols of Buddhism, these structures are monastic or holy places
 
• They also serve as a sacred land that has the power to purify one’s soul.

Nagara architecture

 
• It is the style of temple architecture that became popular in northern India.
 
• In North India, it is common for an entire temple to be built on a stone platform with steps leading up to it.
 
• In South India, it usually has elaborate boundary walls or gateways.
 
• Latina was the most common name for the simple shikhara which is square at the base and whose walls curve or slope inward to a point on top.
 
• The second major type of architectural form in the Nagara order is the phamsana.
 
 
• Phamsana buildings tend to be broader and shorter than Latina ones.
 
• Their roofs are composed of several slabs that gently rise to a single point over the centre of the building, unlike the Latina ones which look like sharply rising tall towers.
 
• Phamsana roofs do not curve inward, instead, they slope upwards on a straight incline.
 
• Phamsana design is used for the mandapas while the main garbhagriha is housed in a Latina building.

questions.question: The rock - cave temple of ______ is the largest monolithic structure in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ellora.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **rock-cave temple** referred to in the question is the **Kailasa Temple** located in the **Ellora Caves complex **in **Maharashtra, India.**
 
• The Kailasa Temple was carved out of a **single rock **in the** 8th century AD **and is considered a marvel of **Indian rock-cut architecture.**
 
• The temple complex covers an area of** 2 acres** and is **164 feet wide, **109 feet long, and 98 feet high.
 
• The temple features intricate carvings and sculptures depicting **Hindu mythology** and is dedicated to Lord Shiva.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Udayagiri caverns** are a group of **20 rock-cut caverns** close to **Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh.**

 
 
• They have been largely associated with the** Hindu gods Vishnu and Shiva** from the early **5th century CE. **
 
 
 
• **The 29 Buddhist cave monuments** known as the **Ajanta Caves** are located in the Maharashtra state's** Aurangabad District.**
 
 
• **​They** date from the second century **BCE to roughly 480 CE.**
 
 
 
• The **Badami cave temples** are situated in the town of Badami in **Karnataka, **India's north-central region.
 
 
• **Hindu and Jain** cave temples can be found together in the **Badami cave templ**e complex.

questions.question: Which of the following temples is NOT an example of Nagara style of architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kailasha temple, Kanchipuram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kailasha temple in Kanchipuram is a fine example of Dravidian architecture, not Nagara style.
 
• Dravidian architecture is predominant in the southern part of India, whereas Nagara style is prevalent in the northern regions.
 
• The Kailasha temple, also known as Kanchi Kailasanathar Temple, was built by the Pallava dynasty.
 
• It features a distinct vimana (tower) over the sanctum and intricate carvings typical of Dravidian architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara Style of Architecture**

 
 
• Prevalent in the northern part of India.
 
• Characterized by beehive-shaped towers called shikharas.
 
• Examples include Lingaraja Temple (Bhubaneswar), Kandariya Mahadeva Temple (Madhya Pradesh), and Sun Temple (Konark).
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Style of Architecture**
 
 
• Predominantly found in southern India.
 
• Features include massive gopurams (gateway towers) and vimanas.
 
• Examples include the Brihadeeswarar Temple (Thanjavur) and Meenakshi Temple (Madurai).
 
 
 
• **Vesara Style of Architecture**
 
 
• A hybrid style that combines elements of both Nagara and Dravidian architecture.
 
• Found primarily in the Deccan region.
 
• Examples include the temples of the Chalukya and Hoysala dynasties.
 
 
 
• **Pallava Dynasty**
 
 
• Ruled parts of southern India from the 4th to the 9th centuries CE.
 
• Known for their contributions to Dravidian architecture.
 
• Built many rock-cut temples and structural temples, including the Kailasha temple in Kanchipuram.

questions.question: In which state is the famous Brihadeshwar temple situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Tamil Nadu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Brihadeshwar Temple** is located in Thanjavur, **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It is also known as **Rajarajeswaram** or **Peruvudaiyār Kōvil**.
 
• This temple is a brilliant example of the major heights achieved in **Chola architecture**, painting, and bronze casting.
 
• The temple was built by **Chola emperor Raja Raja Chola I** in 1010 AD.
 
• It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, known for its architectural grandeur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **vimana** (temple tower) is 216 ft high and is among the tallest of its kind in the world.
 
• The temple has a massive **Shivalinga** in the main sanctum, which is a central figure in the worship practices there.
 
• One of the most astonishing features of the temple is the **shadow of the gopuram (tower)**, which never falls on the ground at noon during any part of the year.
 
• The walls of the temple are covered in detailed **bas-relief** and murals that tell various stories of Shiva, as well as other Hindu deities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** **The Dravidian style of temple architecture**

 
• Dravidian temples are typically **enclosed within a compound wall**, creating a sacred precinct.
 
• The entrance gateway, known as the **gopuram**, is a prominent feature. These towering structures are often elaborately decorated and serve as the main entrance to the temple complex.
 
• The main temple tower, called the vimana, is usually a stepped **pyramid that rises geometrically.** Unlike the curving shikhara of North Indian temples, the vimana has a more angular, tiered appearance.
 
• Many Dravidian temples include a large** water reservoir or temple tank** within the complex, used for ritual purification.
 
• The temples are adorned with detailed carvings depicting various deities,** mythological scenes,** and floral patterns.
 
• 
 
 Nandi is typically placed in mandapa (pavilion) directly facing the main shrine of Lord Shiva.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e41f044d4d5a6a4b8983a4538cbd84e3a80d8ce76ec4fc0af928016fad6d1f3b.png]

questions.question: The architectural marvels, temples of Gangaikonda-Cholapuram, were built by which of the following king?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**King Rajendra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• King Rajendra Chola I was the son and successor of Rajaraja Chola I.
 
• He ruled the Chola dynasty in South India from 1014 to 1044 CE.
 
• Gangaikonda-Cholapuram was established as the capital by Rajendra Chola I after his victorious expedition to the Ganges River.
 
• The temple at Gangaikonda-Cholapuram is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is renowned for its grand architecture and intricate sculptures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chola Dynasty**

 
 
• The Chola Dynasty was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in Southern India, spanning from the 9th to the 13th centuries.
 
• The dynasty is known for its significant contributions to Tamil culture, art, and architecture.
 
• The Cholas expanded their influence across South East Asia, including parts of Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and Indonesia.
 
• The Chola period is often regarded as a golden age for Tamil literature and temple architecture.
 
 
 
• **Gangaikonda-Cholapuram Temple**
 
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is known for its massive lingam, which is one of the largest in India.
 
• It was built to commemorate Rajendra Chola's victory over the Pala Dynasty and his subsequent expedition to the Ganges River.
 
• The architectural style is Dravidian, and the temple complex includes a large Nandi statue and intricately carved pillars.
 
• The temple is often compared to the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur, another masterpiece of Chola architecture.
